title: One writing step on a scanned tape
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $x,w$ be finite words over a symbol type, choose a tape index $i<k$, a machine $M$, a configuration $d$, states $q,q'$, an input-head position $p$, an input movement $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and a natural number $r<|w|$. Form the configuration that has state $q$, input-head position $p$, and the first $r$ symbols of $w$ written consecutively on tape $i$ from its original head position, with the head advanced by $r$. If $M$'s transition on that configuration is to move the input head by $m$, write the $r$th symbol of $w$ at the scanned work-tape cell, move tape $i$ right, and enter state $q'$, then one step of $M$ yields the corresponding configuration with state $q'$, input-head position moved from $p$ by $m$, and the written prefix extended to length $r+1$ with its head advanced by $r+1$.
hypotheses_covered: transition of $M$ on the specified configuration equals the stated write-and-move action
